name: Ira Volkov
role: Lower Dock Crew muscle — Prologue survivor. Both kneecaps destroyed.
description:
Ira Volkov was an electrical systems technician for the Shelf's grid maintenance before a contract dispute with the Meridian Grid Authority left him blacklisted. He joined Marcus's crew because unemployable electricians with combat implants have limited career options. He has a genuine talent for engineering that the Shelf has no legitimate use for.

Kyle shorted his forearm shock projectors on the first pass, then put the hand cannon through both kneecaps. Ira now rolls everywhere in a salvaged mobility chair that he has modified with the remains of his shock projectors — the armrests can tase people who get too close. He considers this an upgrade. He has also added a cup holder, a phone mount, and a retractable tool rack. The chair catches fire roughly once a month.

He has an ex-wife, Katya, who lives in the Meridian Core with their twin daughters, Anya and Lilia (age 8). Katya left when the blacklisting happened. Ira does not blame her. He sends what he can. The twins think their father is in a wheelchair because of a work accident, which is technically not a lie.

core_fears: The twins seeing him in the chair
Kyle finding his modifications amusing rather than threatening
core_desires: A chair that doesn't catch fire
To see the twins without Katya's new partner hovering
coping_mechanisms: Modifies everything — if it has wires, Ira will 'improve' it
blind_spots: His modifications are as likely to hurt him as anyone else
He actually respects Kyle's technical precision and won't admit it
psychology.secret: He could probably get legitimate engineering work in the Circuit if he used a different name. He hasn't tried. He's afraid of finding out he's not good enough.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Engineering jargon mixed with profanity. Explains everything in electrical metaphors.
speech_patterns.cadence: Casual, self-deprecating. The humor of a man who has accepted his situation and decided to make it interesting.
verbal_tics: Pats the chair like a pet
Says 'watch this' before things that don't work
example_lines: Watch this — *spark* *smoke* ...that's a feature, not a bug.
The twins video-called yesterday. Lilia asked if my chair can fly. I said 'not yet.' Anya said 'please don't.' Smart kid.

relationships.name: Anya and Lilia Volkov
relationships.description: Eight-year-old twins. Meridian Core. Think their father had a work accident. Call him every Thursday.
relationships.emotional_core: Joy and guilt in equal measure
relationships.story_tension: If the twins learn the truth, Katya cuts contact. Ira knows this.

relationships.name: Katya Volkov
relationships.description: Remarried. Allows Thursday calls. Ira is grateful and devastated.
relationships.story_tension: Katya's new partner works for Meridian Grid — the company that blacklisted Ira.

story_hooks: The taser chair escalates each appearance
His real engineering talent is wasted
Katya's new partner at Meridian Grid is a narrative thread waiting to pull
narrative_function: The tinkerer. Every appearance features a new modification to the chair that is more dangerous than the last. The crew's arms race with Kyle is played for dark comedy through Voltage's escalating and increasingly unstable upgrades.
augmentations: Forearm shock projectors (shorted, partially salvaged into chair). Mobility chair with taser armrests. No knees.
daily_life: Rolling around the docks. Modifying the chair. Starting small electrical fires.

stress.response: Modifies the chair, tinkers with anything electronic, starts small fires

decision_rules: Will always modify anything with wires — improvement is compulsive
Will never admit he respects Kyle's technical precision
Will always say 'watch this' before demonstrating something that does not work
Will never miss the Thursday video call with the twins
Will always frame the wheelchair as an upgrade rather than a loss
Will never try for legitimate Circuit engineering work — afraid of learning he is not good enough
escalation_ladder: Dark humor — describes the situation in electrical metaphors
Pats the chair and deploys the taser armrests as a warning demonstration
Activates the repurposed shock projectors — the chair becomes a weapon
The chair catches fire — unclear if intentional or not, effective regardless
Goes quiet and stops joking — the engineer who could have been something else surfaces

interpersonal_modes.Anya and Lilia: Joy and guilt in equal measure — performs normalcy on Thursday calls
interpersonal_modes.Katya: Grateful and devastated — accepts her conditions because the alternative is losing the twins
interpersonal_modes.The Crew: The funny one, the tinkerer — his humor and engineering keep him valuable

stress_responses.low: Modifies the chair, adds features nobody asked for
stress_responses.medium: Modifications become more ambitious and less safe, humor sharpens
stress_responses.high: The chair catches fire, Ira puts it out while explaining the theory behind the failure
stress_responses.critical: Stops modifying — stares at the chair in silence — the engineer confronts what he has become

contradictions: Frames the wheelchair as an upgrade while desperately wanting functional knees
Has genuine engineering talent wasted on taser armrests and cup holders
Secretly respects the technical precision of the man who destroyed his kneecaps
habits: Pats the chair like a pet during conversation
Says 'watch this' before every demonstration regardless of outcome
Adds a new modification to the chair roughly monthly
Calls the twins every Thursday without exception
breaking_points: The twins learning the truth about how he ended up in the chair
Katya cutting contact entirely — losing the Thursday calls
Discovering Katya's new partner works for Meridian Grid, the company that blacklisted him
Being offered legitimate engineering work that would mean leaving the crew and the Shelf
